mission.title: Mission Brief
mission.body: Explorer, welcome to New Orleans. Every city leaves behind clues. Some are found in famous landmarks. Others are hidden in the food people eat, the music they play, and the stories they continue to tell. Your assignment is to investigate this city and record your discoveries.
objectives: Decide whether the local legend is believable.

food.title: Local Flavor
food.intro: Some cities are remembered by their landmarks. New Orleans is remembered by its flavors.

items.name: Beignets
items.description: Deep-fried pastries covered with powdered sugar. Best enjoyed with coffee.

items.name: Gumbo
items.description: A rich stew influenced by French, African, Spanish, and Native American cooking.

items.name: Muffuletta
items.description: A famous New Orleans sandwich filled with meats, cheese, and olive salad.

food.question: Which food would you try first?

culture.title: Culture & Traditions
culture.intro: The heart of New Orleans can be found in its music, celebrations, neighborhoods, and river history.

items.title: Jazz
items.description: New Orleans is widely considered the birthplace of jazz. Musicians still perform throughout the city every day.

items.title: Mardi Gras
items.description: Every spring, colorful parades, floats, costumes, and music transform New Orleans into one giant festival.

items.title: French Quarter
items.description: Historic balconies, hidden courtyards, and narrow streets preserve centuries of history.

items.title: Mississippi River
items.description: The river made New Orleans one of America's most important ports and connected the city to the entire continent.

culture.blakeNote: I followed the sound of a trumpet for three blocks before realizing I had no idea where I was anymore. Best wrong turn I've made in a while.

blake.title: Dear Explorer
paragraphs: I was about to buy another beignet when I noticed the receipt said "Parish Tax."
Louisiana doesn't use counties like most states—it uses parishes, a tradition dating back to the state's French and Spanish colonial history.
The jazz is impossible to ignore. So is the smell of fresh bread.

legend.title: Local Legend
legend.name: The Casket Girls
legend.body: In the early 1700s, young women known as the Casket Girls arrived in New Orleans carrying small chests of belongings. Later generations claimed those chests contained something far more mysterious. Locals still tell stories about the attic windows of the old convent remaining sealed.

archive.title: Archive Record
archive.note: The street grid of the French Quarter still follows many of its original eighteenth-century plans. Some buildings have changed. The streets mostly haven't.
